newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Alcatel jumps on bullish outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Alcatel jumps on bullish outlook.

text.p: Shares in Alcatel Alsthom SA jumped by more than 11 percent on Tuesday to a new high as financial analysts upgraded their profit forecasts after a bullish presentation of 1996 results.

Alcatel, France's biggest industrial group, reported a small profit for 1996 after an historic loss in 1995, and chairman Serge Tchuruk told a news conference that Alcatel should make satisfactory profits in 1998.

Alcatel on Tuesday turned in net attributable profit of 2.7 billion francs ($473 million) for 1996 compared with a loss of 25.6 billion francs in 1995. Sales rose to 162.1 billion francs in 1996 from 160.4 billion the year before.

It raised its net dividend to 10 francs per share, from eight francs in 1995, but the payout remained below the 14 francs it paid in the three years to 1994. Debt fell sharply, with gearing at 32 percent from 61 percent in 1995.

The share closed at 667 francs, up 8.81 percent, after a high of 682 francs for a 11.3 percent jump -- its highest level since 1994 when telecoms orders fell sharply and pulled the share 46 percent down from an all-time high of 913 francs in January to a low of 408 at the end of that year.
The Paris CAC-40 blue-chip index closed 0.56 percent down.
Tchuruk said Alcatel planned to create a major defence group if it wins a bidding war for state defence electronics group Thomson-CSF against Lagardere.
He also said the company is talking to Britain's GEC Plc about extending cooperation beyond their GEC Alsthom transport and power generation joint venture.

Tchuruk said the core telecommunications would be boosted enormously by the explosion in Internet use, especially because the company aimed to have a system ready in 1998 which would help speed up the net and make an end to the "World Wide Wait" on the world-wide web of computer connections.

Analysts said Tchuruk told a results briefing that operating margins of eight to 10 percent were possible and brokers said that some financial houses were increasing their 1998 profit forecast to 50 francs per share, or eight billion francs, from some 42 francs previously.

"What counts is 1998 and there the outlook is exceptional," an analyst said. "Tchuruk presented Alcatel Alsthom as an Internet (related) stock, which pleased investors who had not tought about that before," another analyst said.

Tchuruk told a news conference that the group had sold assets worth 15.4 billion francs, cut its legal structure by half to 500 units and had reorganised the group into profit centres and clear divisions.
He warned there could be further job cuts in 1997 and early 1998 after 14,500 people were axed in 1995 and 1996. Alcatel employed some 190,000 people at the end of 1996.
Tchuruk said the Alcatel's core activities would be telecoms, cables and components as well as engineering and systems with total sales of 200 billion francs a year.
Telecoms would account for more than 85 percent of sales and would see rapid growth due to the rise in mobile telecoms and Internet use.
Alcatel is bidding with Dassault Industrie for the state's 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF and counts Aerospatiale among its allies to create a 60 billion franc group.
The French government will announce the winner in June.
Tchuruk said he planned defence ventures with both GEC and Germany's DASA if Alcatel won the Thomson price.
